div.p: Mimic defense techniques can solve unknown vulnerabilities as well as backdoors without prior knowledge based on DHR structure. Compared with traditional defense methods, DHR structure brings dynamic and heterogeneous factors into systems to enhance security. In this paper, we discuss the security-critical scheduling problem in DHR-based processing system and propose MHF algorithm according to the characters of heterogeneous processing nodes with different performance. While ensuring task schedulability, MHF algorithm improves the average heterogeneity of processing nodes as high as possible when allocating redundant versions of a task. Simulation results show that the average heterogeneity of MHF algorithm is 22.7% higher than that of RF algorithm when tasks' guarantee ratio approaches 100%.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Real-time systems are widely used in industrial control, aviation and other fields to ensure reliable results within a specified time range. In recent years, frequent security events demonstrate that security threats are becoming increasingly serious in industrial control and many other fields. However, industrial control systems may overlook security factors for enhancing availability. Meanwhile, traditional defense techniques rely on priori knowledge and are still vulnerable to advanced sophisticated attacks with static and deterministic characteristics [1] [2]. These factors all aggravate the security situation.

Mimic defense technique provides a possibility for solving the above problems. It bases on DHR (dynamic heterogeneous redundancy) structure and can change the defense scenario, building a highly credible and reliable system with untrusted components. Utilizing generalized stochastic Petri net model, Wu Jiangxing [3] has proved that triple-redundant DHR-based systems can obtain lower escape probability and higher exception perception probability than non-redundant systems and dissimilar redundant systems, in which output dissimilarity, failure generation rate and recovery rate play a key role.

Present discussions in mimic defense techniques are mainly about applying this theory in multiple fields and discuss how much it enhances security with dynamically changing heterogeneous environment. Under the DHR structure, this paper is mainly about scheduling tasks in heterogeneous processing systems to meet the real-time requirement and achieve security gains.

The rest of the paper is organized as follows. Section II describes background and related work. Section III introduces related models and a security-critical scheduling algorithm is proposed in section IV. Section V compares our algorithm with the widely used RF algorithm in simulations. Finally, section VI describes conclusions and future work.

div.head: II. BACKGROUND AND RELATED WORK
div.p: Existing researches on security-critical real-time scheduling are mainly about distributed systems (such as clusters), and provide high level security services as much as possible under the condition of guaranteeing real-time performance. Tao Xie et al. [4] propose a security overhead model about confidentiality, integrity and authentication services in cluster, as well as a security-aware heuristic strategy called SAREC; Zhu Xiaomin et al. [5] propose a two-stage adaptive scheduling strategy called TPSS, meeting both security and real-time demands, based on the overhead model [4]. In the wireless network environment, Zhu Xiaomin et al. [6] propose a security-aware algorithm ISAPS to assign different level security services according to workload changes in connection. The above discussions are mainly relied on the existing security services. Once system vulnerabilities or backdoors are found, it is difficult to ensure its credibility or reliability.

The utilizations of redundancy are also discussed in realtime scheduling to enhance reliability. Manimaran et al. [7] propose a scheduling algorithm to meet multiple-mission requirements in multiprocessor systems, supporting different fault-tolerant techniques (TMR, Primary Backup, and Imprecise Computation). Chernigovskiy et al. [8] discuss how to reduce execution time to run the N-version software of the control system in satellite. Saito et al. [9] consider both system reliability and overhead, determining the number of cores allocated for a task according to the "fault pattern". Redundancy is mainly to improve reliability rather than security. This paper bases on DHR structure which brings dynamic and heterogeneous factors by implementing voting techniques and variable defense scenarios.

div.head: A. Scheduler Model
div.p: This paper proposes a centralized scheduling structure according to DHR and the model is illustrated in Figure 1. The structure includes a task scheduler, a switching controller and voter. The task scheduler communicates with the local scheduler of each processing node to obtain realtime feedback information, including workload, task security requirements, output conditions, etc. Tasks are then assigned to local queues of appropriate processing nodes with the task order adjusted in real time. The switching controller will make abnormal nodes with continuous failure go offline while choose a normal one instead. Details of switching will not be discussed in this paper. Voter and voting queue are mainly used to deal with asynchronous outputs of a task from different local queues. Considering security and system versatility, task-level synchronization ensures that each node will process tasks independently without sending messages to others.

A task first arrives at global input queue, and will be replicated and inserted into a particular set of local queues after task scheduler determines whether the task satisfies schedulability and security( the number of redundant versions, etc.) requirements. Otherwise, the task will be discarded into the rejected queue. According to feedback information, the task scheduler can adjust execution orders of tasks or discard some tasks in the local queues by local schedulers before a task enters the corresponding processing node. The final result of a task will be given after its outputs reaches agreement.

where stij denotes start time of task ti on node j. ei is the execution time matrix of task ti where eij denotes execution time of task ti on node j. Although the concept of 'heterogeneity' in DHR structure is focus on differences in function realization under the equivalent functional conditions and is related to security, we assume that heterogeneous nodes will generate different execution time for one task and this difference is independent of this 'realization difference'. The 'realization difference' will be defined in part C of section III. ini and outi denote task input time( such as task replication time) and output time( such as voting time), and we simplify these two variables as predictable fixed values. di denote the deadline of ti.
Tasks in this paper are all non-preemptive and can't be suspended or rejected after entering processing nodes. Task scheduler tries to ensure that local input queues are filled with waiting tasks.

div.head: C. Node Model
div.p: In DHR structure, heterogeneity ensures that attackers can't exploit the vulnerabilities or backdoors in multiple processing nodes at the same time, and can perceive abnormal outputs by voting. It is difficult for an attacker to successfully control a system by limited execution of tasks. Heterogeneity under equivalent functional conditions can be implemented in both software and hardware, and generated from diverse designs (like N-versions), or from different vendors. Benoit and Martin [10] summarize researches of software diversity and divide it into multiple dimensions, such as design diversity, natural diversity and automatic diversity. Diversity is expected to avoid common-mode failure for reliability or security and its validity has been supported by a large number of studies. Michael et al. [11] try to quantify software diversity through structure, error distribution and tough stages in software development and introduce some metrics like unique operator numbers, unique operand numbers, etc.

Modeling and measuring heterogeneity are not the focus of this paper, but are related to our scheduling strategy. A simple description of heterogeneity between processing nodes is given referring to the literature [12] [13].

For any task, ni and nj will not output identical abnormal results if hij is equal to 1.

Under actual circumstance, for example, the heterogeneity between hardware components from different vendors can be small while it is the opposite if components are from identical vendors. Therefore, a parameter called Heterogeneity Category is proposed to characterize the heterogeneity classification number in section V and dominate the generation of general heterogeneity matrix.

div.head: IV. MHF ALGORITHM
div.p: A DHR-based task scheduling algorithm MHF (Maximum Heterogeneity First) is proposed in this session. The main idea of MHF is to find a low-complexity task allocation scheme meeting deadlines and maximizing the average heterogeneity (this will be introduced below) in the system with N nodes. Considering that allocating redundant versions of tasks to relatively fixed node combinations may harm security, it is necessary to avoid the situation. Meanwhile redundancy can reduce schedulability in system [7], and discarding some tasks in local queues is required to guarantee the successful allocation of tasks in system. However, it will consume large amount of space to store the results of node combinations as well as related parameters when there are many nodes in the system and arriving tasks require different numbers of redundant versions. Node initialization is meant to solve the problem by generating a node set with a randomly chosen node for a task.

div.head: B. Simulation Results and Analyses
div.p: Figure 3 illustrates impacts of task arrival time on performance. We evaluate algorithms by GR( guarantee ratio) and ART( average response time). As illustrated in Figure 3(a), to let the GR approach 1, the average time interval ( i.e. 1 λ ) in MHF need exceed 100 while that in RF need exceed 80. This slight difference is mainly due to the fact that RF algorithm in the redundant execution scenario simply takes the number of task versions into account without considering the effect of heterogeneity. Based on the results from Figure 3(a), 1 λ starts from 100 ( to ensure GR approaches 1) in Figure 3(b). It is obvious that maximum-heterogeneity-first strategy has a significant impact on ART with the mean ART of MHF 94.7% higher than that of RF when 1 λ varies from 100 to 140. This value will decrease to approximately 30.1% when referring to fast-voting MHF and RF. Considering that GR is close to 1, the system still meets the real-time requirement. Figure 4 illustrates the impact of node numbers on the average heterogeneity when 1 λ equals 100. The average heterogeneity of MHF is slightly higher than that of fastvoting MHF and the value of both will increase with the number of processing nodes. It is mainly because the node selection ranges of different Heterogeneity Categories expand. In contrast, the average heterogeneity of RF has little to do with the number of nodes. In general, the average heterogeneity of MHF is approximately 22.7% higher than that of RF with node numbers ranging from 12 to 20.

Figure 5 illustrates the impact of diversity categories on the average heterogeneity when node number equals 12. Based on the result that the utilization of 2-out-of-3 voting algorithm does not significantly reduce the average heterogeneity, only MHF and RF will be discussed in Figure 5. As defined in part C of session III, Heterogeneity Category affects differences of heterogeneity. In Figure 5, both MHF and RF increase with the number of Heterogeneity Category, the average heterogeneity of MHF remaining approximately 18.4% higher than that of RF. Essentially, the increase comes from the raise of heterogeneity between nodes in the heterogeneity matrix.

div.head: VI. CONCLUSION AND FUTURE WORK
div.p: Existing security-critical scheduling researches neglect that dynamic and heterogeneous factors can help solving flaws and backdoors. This paper discusses security-critical real-time scheduling under DHR structure and proposes MHF algorithm allocating tasks within deadlines and maximizing the average heterogeneity for security. Simulations and analyses demonstrate that the proposed MHF algorithm has limited effects on schedulability with the average heterogeneity increasing 22.7% compared with RF algorithm. The average heterogeneity increases with the system's node numbers and heterogeneity classification numbers.
Our future work is to discuss real-time scheduling considering the component switching process in DHR structure.
